title: Cybersecurity Analyst
tagline: Defend organisations: detect attacks, respond to incidents, harden systems.
about: Security analysts (the 'blue team') protect organisations. In a Security Operations Centre you'll triage alerts, investigate suspicious activity, respond to incidents and improve detections so the next attack is caught sooner.
Demand is persistent across every industry and government. Curiosity, calm under pressure and clear writing matter as much as tools.
day: Investigate suspicious logins, processes and network traffic
Respond to incidents and write reports
Tune detections and reduce false positives

phases.title: Security foundations
phases.goal: Know how computers and networks work well enough to defend them.

nodes.d: Security is mostly networking. Know how packets get from A to B and what each layer does.
Most servers and security tools run on Linux. Get comfortable at the command line.
links: OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Most corporate networks run Windows with Active Directory, and most breaches touch it.
Python and Bash to automate tasks, parse logs and write small tools.
The vocabulary: CIA triad, threats vs vulnerabilities vs risks, defence in depth, least privilege.
What hashing, encryption and signatures do, and how they go wrong.

project.d: Build a virtual lab: a Linux server, a Windows machine and a firewall in VirtualBox or Proxmox. Document the network diagram and harden each machine with a checklist.

phases.title: Blue-team skills
phases.goal: See attacks in logs and traffic.

nodes.d: Collect, search and correlate logs across an organisation.
Read packet captures and spot anomalies.
What attackers do on a machine and how EDR and Sysmon record it.
A shared map of attacker tactics and techniques; the language of detection.
Write detections as code and test them against real attack data.
The most common way in. Analyse emails, headers, links and attachments safely.

project.d: Send logs from your home lab to an open-source SIEM (Elastic or Wazuh), simulate five ATT&CK techniques, and write detections that catch each one with low false positives.

phases.title: Incident response & governance
phases.goal: Handle incidents end to end and speak the language of risk.

nodes.d: Preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned.
Collect and analyse evidence from disks, memory and logs.
Use indicators and reports to anticipate attacks.
Find, prioritise and track fixes for vulnerabilities.
Frameworks and regulations that shape security programmes.
Identity, logging and misconfigurations in AWS/Azure.

project.d: Investigate a public practice incident (for example a Blue Team Labs or LetsDefend case) and write a professional report: timeline, impact, root cause and recommendations.

nodes.d: Proactively search for attackers that evaded detection.
Static and dynamic analysis in a safe lab.
Automate repetitive triage with Python and playbooks.
Keep skills sharp with defensive and forensic CTFs.

interview: Walk through investigating a suspicious login or a phishing email.
Networking: TCP handshake, DNS, common ports and protocols.
Explain ATT&CK techniques and how you'd detect one.
Scenario: ransomware on one laptop. What do you do in the first hour?
certs: CompTIA CySA+ or Blue Team Level 1
